case1_no_timeout.fault: latency: 3s on dep:9090, at: peak for: 15s
case1_no_timeout.candidates_reason: target 'dep' is a custom image outside detect's closed vocabulary, so it never becomes a detect.Dep; even if it did, clientKnobPatterns has no net/http entry (noted since round 1).

case2_retry_storm.defect: Retry with no cap or backoff
case2_retry_storm.fault: down: true on dep:9090, at: peak for: 15s
case2_retry_storm.candidates_reason: same as case 1 (custom dep image); also the retry loop itself is hand-rolled, not a library detect could recognize even in principle.

case3_pool_exhaustion.defect: Connection pool of 5 (pgxpool.MaxConns) behind load needing far more concurrency
case3_pool_exhaustion.fault: none -- load-only defect, no faults: entry
case3_pool_exhaustion.candidates_reason: STRUCTURAL: internal/run/findings.go's attribute() only ever appends candidates by iterating cfg.Faults; with zero faults declared (the correct, honest torture.yaml for a pure load-induced defect), the loop never runs, so candidates are never populated even though postgres/pgx IS in detect's vocabulary and clientKnobPatterns DOES have a 'jackc/pgx' entry (MaxConns, MinConns, ConnConfig.ConnectTimeout) that would have been exactly right. Confirmed empirically: no candidates field appears despite a real pgx dependency being present and detectable. This means D-9 candidates can never surface for the entire class of defect (3, 6, 7 in this corpus) that manifests from load alone rather than an injected fault -- which is exactly how BENCHMARKS.md describes cases 3, 6 and 7.

case5_no_circuit_breaker.defect: No circuit breaker on the cascade path; a shared, small worker-slot pool lets a slow dependency call starve unrelated traffic
case5_no_circuit_breaker.fault: latency: 3s on dep:9090, at: peak for: 15s
case5_no_circuit_breaker.cascade_confirmed_live: Curled /health (a route that calls no dependency at all) from inside the SUT's own network namespace during the fault window: 5.37s response time -- direct proof the shared worker pool, not just the /checkout path, was saturated. This is the actual case-5 signature (a slow dep taking the whole service down), not just case 1 repeated.

case6_unbounded_queue.defect: Unbounded in-memory queue drained far slower than it fills
case6_unbounded_queue.fault: none -- load-only defect, sustained spike against a capacity-limited container (mem_limit: 24m)
case6_unbounded_queue.candidates_reason: same structural gap as case 3 -- no fault, so attribute() never runs.
case6_unbounded_queue.root_cause_confirmed: docker inspect on the container after the run: OOMKilled=true, ExitCode=137. First attempt at this fixture (mem_limit 64m, un-written byte slices) did NOT trigger an OOM despite 'logically' queuing hundreds of MB, because a make([]byte, N) slice that is never written to can sit on the kernel's shared zero page and never become resident (confirmed via docker stats showing RSS far below the queued total) -- cgroup memory accounting, and the OOM killer, only see real, written pages. Fixed the fixture (fills every byte) and tightened the limit to 24m; this is a fixture-calibration fix, not a softening of the defect -- the defect (no queue cap) is unchanged.

case7_cache_stampede.defect: Cache-aside read with a short TTL and no stampede protection
case7_cache_stampede.fault: none -- load-only defect, periodic TTL boundary under sustained concurrent load
case7_cache_stampede.candidates_reason: same structural gap as case 3 -- no fault, so attribute() never runs, even though redis/go-redis is a recognized dependency+client.

case4_nonidempotent_consumer.reason: Requires a message broker (Kafka/Redpanda), a Kafka REST Proxy-compatible endpoint (internal/applier.BrokerApplier's actual driven interface), consumer-group semantics, and -broker-url wiring through cmd/tortureu -- materially more infrastructure than the other five cases. Judged not to fit this round's remaining budget. Recorded as unmeasured, not attempted with a shortcut that would misrepresent the result.

metrics.detection: 6/6 measurable planted defects detected (cases 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7). Case 4 unmeasured (not built). Case 8 (control) correctly found nothing.
metrics.attribution: 3/3 fault-driven cases (1, 2, 5) named the correct causing fault (Cause.fault matched the planted fault's name and target exactly). Cases 3, 6, 7 are load-only defects with no injected fault -- Cause is structurally never populated for these (attribute() only fires per-fault), so 'named the correct causing fault' does not apply to them; not counted as either a hit or a miss, reported as not applicable.
metrics.candidates: 0/6 findings carried a candidate list, across every case. Root cause is structural, not per-case: internal/run/findings.go's attribute() only attaches D-9 candidates by walking cfg.Faults, so a load-only defect (cases 3, 6, 7) NEVER gets a candidate list even when the target dependency and its client library are both in detect's recognized vocabulary (confirmed directly for case 3's postgres/pgx and case 7's redis/go-redis, both of which have real entries in clientKnobPatterns). For the fault-driven cases (1, 2, 5), the gap is the one found in round 1: the target is a custom application service outside detect's closed image vocabulary, so it never becomes a detect.Dep at all.
metrics.false_positive_on_control: 0, across 17 consecutive case-8 runs spanning three different code-path states (post-classification-fix, post-exit-code-fix). This is the number the whole eval was built to get right, and it has stayed at zero every time it was actually measured.
